:::{#thm-data-processing-inequality}
#### Data processing inequality

If $X \to Y \to Z$ is a [Markov chain](#def-markov-chain)
and the entropies of $X$, $Y$ and $Z$ are finite, <!-- check-term-links: allow -->
then

$$I(X; Z) \le I(X; Y).$$

:::

::: {.proof}

The [chain rule](#thm-mutual-information-chain-rule) for the pair $(Z, Y)$ and the pair $(Y, Z)$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
I(Z, Y; X) &= I(Y; X) + I(Z; X \mid Y) \\
I(Y, Z; X) &= I(Z; X) + I(Y; X \mid Z).
\end{aligned}
$$

The pairs $(Z, Y)$ and $(Y, Z)$ list the same two values in a different order,
so they have the same joint distribution up to relabelling,
and the left sides are equal.
By @lem-markov-chain-conditional-mutual-information, $I(Z; X \mid Y) = 0$.
By @thm-conditional-mutual-information-nonnegative, $I(Y; X \mid Z) \ge 0$.
Equating the left sides gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
I(Y; X)
&= I(Z; X) + I(Y; X \mid Z) \\
&\ge I(Z; X).
\end{aligned}
$$

By @thm-mutual-information-symmetric,
$I(Y; X) = I(X; Y)$ and $I(Z; X) = I(X; Z)$,
so $I(X; Z) \le I(X; Y)$.

:::
